Despite attempts from Cercle Brugge to respond, Zulte Waregem 's defense held firm. The first booking of the match came in the 43rd minute, as Anosike Ementa of Zulte Waregem received a yellow card. Second Half Erupts with Goals and a Comeback Following the interval, Cercle Brugge emerged with renewed purpose. Their comeback began in the 57th minute when Jeppe Erenbjerg equalized for the hosts. The momentum shifted dramatically just two minutes later, in the 65th minute, as Dante Vanzeir , assisted by Pieter Gerkens , fired Cercle Brugge into the lead, sending the stadium into a frenzy. However, Zulte Waregem showed resilience and fought back to level the scores in the 67th minute through Marley Ake , reigniting their hopes. Opoku's Late Strike Decides Tense Encounter Substitutions were made by both sides as they looked to gain an edge in a fiercely contested second half. As the clock ticked down, the tension was palpable. Then, in the 88th minute, Cercle Brugge found the decisive blow. Joseph Opoku became the hero for the home side, scoring the winning goal after a superb assist from Serxho Ujka . The stadium erupted in celebration as the late goal sealed a dramatic victory for Cercle Brugge . After a few minutes of added time, the referee blew the final whistle, bringing an end to a memorable and hard-fought contest.

High-stakes football returned to the forefront on April 27, 2026 , as Zulte Waregem welcomed RAAL La Louvière for a clash that promised tactical intrigue and individual brilliance. The encounter in the Jupiler Pro League offered both sides a chance to assert their dominance in a high-pressure environment. Erenbjerg Ignites the Opening Exchange The match began with a palpable energy as the hosts looked to establish control of the tempo from the opening whistle. It did not take long for the pressure to yield results, as Jeppe Erenbjerg found the back of the net in the 13th minute to give his side an early advantage. The goal settled the home crowd and forced RAAL La Louvière to rethink their defensive shape early in the first half. As the visitors struggled to find their rhythm, Zulte Waregem continued to exploit gaps in the final third. In the 25th minute, the lead was doubled when Anosike Ementa provided a pinpoint delivery to find Jeppe Erenbjerg once again. The forward made no mistake, clinical in his execution to record his second goal of the afternoon. While RAAL La Louvière attempted to claw their way back into the contest, the half ended with rising tensions, punctuated by a yellow card for Enrique Lofolomo just before the break. Tactical Shifts and Opoku’s Immediate Impact The second half saw both managers turn to their benches in an attempt to shift the momentum. RAAL La Louvière introduced Nachon Nsingi and Pape Moussa Fall immediately after the restart, seeking a spark to ignite a comeback. However, it was a change from the home side in the 63rd minute that would prove to be the masterstroke of the afternoon. Joseph Opoku entered the fray, replacing the veteran Jelle Vossen , and his impact was instantaneous. Within sixty seconds of stepping onto the pitch, Joseph Opoku found the net to extend the lead to three. Once again, it was Anosike Ementa who provided the vital assist, carving open the defense with precision. The goal effectively ended the match as a contest, but the hosts were not finished. In the 74th minute, the same duo combined for a final flourish. Ementa registered his third assist of the match, setting up Opoku for his second goal in just over ten minutes of play, highlighting a devastating partnership that the visitors could not contain. Professional Finish and Final Whistle With the result beyond doubt, the final fifteen minutes saw a series of substitutions as both teams looked toward their next fixtures. Samuel Gueulette received a yellow card for the visitors as frustrations grew, while Zulte Waregem introduced fresh legs in Noah Makembo-Ntemo and Serxho Ujka to see out the closing stages. The home side remained disciplined, maintaining their clean sheet despite late attempts from the opposition to find a consolation goal. When the referee blew the final whistle after four minutes of stoppage time, the story of the match was clear. Through a combination of Anosike Ementa ’s creative vision and the clinical finishing of Jeppe Erenbjerg and Joseph Opoku , Zulte Waregem delivered a statement performance that left the travelling fans with little to cheer about.

The match between Zulte Waregem and Dender , held on May 11, 2026, was a testament to the competitive nature of the Jupiler Pro League . As the clock ticked, both sides fought for every ball, turning the pitch into a theater of high-stakes football. A lively opening period The game kicked off with high intensity, with Laurent Lemoine picking up an early booking in the 17th minute. The deadlock was broken in the 25th minute when Bryan Goncalves stepped up to calmly convert a penalty for FCV Dender EH . However, Zulte Waregem demonstrated resilience, leveling the score through a clinical strike from Marley Ake in the 41st minute. Just as the teams were preparing for the interval, disaster struck. In stoppage time, specifically at the 45+2 minute mark, Bryan Goncalves turned from hero to villain, accidentally putting the ball into his own net. This own goal provided a dramatic shift in momentum, leaving the visitors reeling as they headed into the halftime break. Second half tactical adjustments The restart saw a flurry of activity from the coaching benches as both managers sought to gain the upper hand. Players like Jakob Kiilerich Rask and Enrique Lofolomo were introduced to inject fresh energy into the match. The physical nature of the contest continued into the second half, with the referee busy brandishing yellow cards to Luc Marijnissen , Krzysztof Koton , and Desmond Acquah . Despite late tactical switches, including the introductions of Jeppe Erenbjerg and Stavros Gavriel , neither team could find a way to alter the scoreline again. The final whistle sounded in the 95th minute, ending a match defined by that pivotal moment of misfortune in the dying seconds of the first half.
